title: Gold Demand Trends: US Focus Q2 2026
gist: US total gold demand collapsed to 7.9t in Q2 2026 (-94% y/y, vs a 10-year quarterly average of 90t) entirely because US-listed gold ETFs shed 44.4t, with 61t of H1 outflows concentrated in just two months (March -85t/US$13bn and June -40t/US$5bn); strip those two months out and US ETFs would have taken in 65t of net inflows. Ex-ETF US demand (jewellery + tech + bar and coin) was 52.3t, barely below the 55.8t of a year earlier, and fund-level data show flagship GLD (-US$9.0bn, -65t YTD) and IAU (-US$4.2bn, -29t) bleeding while cheaper GLDM (+US$4.3bn, +28t) and IAUM (+US$837mn, +5t) gained.

insights.claim: Total US gold demand fell to 7.9t in Q2 2026, down 76% q/q and 94% y/y from 126.2t in Q2 2025, and far below the 10-year quarterly average of 90t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The single worst US quarterly demand print in a decade sets the bar for any 'US buyer is back' narrative — watch whether Q3 mean-reverts toward 90t.
insights.quote: Total US gold demand remained under pressure in Q2, falling to 8t, well below its 10-year quarterly average of 90t.
insights.locator: A weak quarter with pockets of resilience

insights.claim: US gold demand totalled 41t in H1 2026 (32.7t in Q1 plus 7.9t in Q2), against second-half 2025 quarters of 193.6t and 172.0t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: H1 2026 US demand ran at roughly a fifth of the H2 2025 pace — a demand air-pocket that any US-flow-based gold thesis has to explain.
insights.quote: This brought total US gold demand to 41t in H1.
insights.locator: US gold demand overshadowed by ETF outflows

insights.claim: Excluding ETFs, US gold demand in Q2 2026 was 52.3t (jewellery 22.2t, technology 16.3t, bar and coin 13.8t) versus 55.8t a year earlier — a roughly 6% y/y decline against the headline's 94% collapse.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Physical and industrial US gold consumption barely moved; the headline number is a pure ETF-flow artefact, so trading it as a consumption signal is a mistake.
insights.locator: Table 1: Quarterly US gold demand by sector, tonnes

insights.claim: US-listed gold ETF demand swung from +70.4t in Q2 2025 to -44.4t in Q2 2026, a 114.8t reversal that more than accounts for the entire 118.3t drop in total US demand.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: ETF flow is the only US variable that matters for the headline print — model it directly rather than tracking retail or jewellery channels.
insights.quote: The decline was driven primarily by continued weakness in US-listed physically backed gold ETFs.
insights.locator: US gold demand overshadowed by ETF outflows

themes.theme: Two liquidation episodes, not a trend

insights.claim: US-listed gold ETF holdings fell 85t in March 2026, equivalent to US$13bn — the largest monthly outflow in US dollar terms on record and the third largest in tonnage terms.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Record dollar-value redemptions mark a positioning flush, historically a setup for exhaustion rather than the start of a structural exit.
insights.quote: This marked the largest monthly outflow in US dollar terms and the third largest in tonnage terms.
insights.locator: ETF weakness was concentrated, not continuous

insights.claim: Within Q2 2026, US gold ETF holdings fell just 4t across April and May combined but a further 40t (US$5bn) in June alone — the third-largest monthly outflow in US dollar terms on record.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Intra-quarter flow was flat until the last month, so month-end/quarter-end windows are where the gold ETF supply hits the tape.
insights.quote: Holdings fell by 40t in June, compared with a combined 4t decline during April and May, reinforcing the pattern of concentrated quarter-end selling that also characterised Q1.
insights.locator: US gold demand overshadowed by ETF outflows

insights.claim: US gold-backed ETFs recorded net outflows of 61t in H1 2026, the fourth largest H1 tonnage decline and the second largest H1 outflow in US dollar terms on record.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The dollar rank being worse than the tonnage rank shows high prices amplify the market impact of any given tonnage redemption — a structural change in how ETF selling transmits.
insights.quote: As a result, US gold backed ETFs recorded net outflows of 61t in H1, marking the fourth largest H1 decline in holdings and the second largest H1 outflow in US dollar terms on record
insights.locator: ETF weakness was concentrated, not continuous

insights.claim: Stripping out the March and June liquidations, US gold-backed ETFs would have recorded 65t of net inflows in H1 2026 rather than 61t of outflows.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Baseline US ETF demand was positive all half — the bearish flow headline overstates real investor abandonment of gold.
insights.quote: Excluding the March and June outflows, US gold backed ETFs would have recorded 65t of net inflows in H1.
insights.locator: ETF weakness was concentrated, not continuous

insights.claim: The largest US gold ETF reductions in both Q1 and Q2 2026 occurred in the final month of the quarter, a repeatable quarter-end liquidation pattern rather than steady attrition.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Treat gold ETF supply as calendar-clustered: fade quarter-end weakness and expect flow to stabilise in the first two months of each quarter.
insights.quote: Importantly, the weakness was highly concentrated with the largest reductions occurring in the final month of each quarter.
insights.locator: ETF weakness was concentrated, not continuous

insights.claim: US gold ETF outflows accelerated in June 2026 even as the gold price was falling, with redemptions themselves reinforcing the downward price move.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A reflexive price-flow loop means gold drawdowns can overshoot on ETF mechanics alone — sizing should assume momentum-driven air pockets.
insights.quote: But outflows gathered momentum in June despite a falling gold price, with holdings declining by a further 40t, equivalent to US$5bn, the third-largest monthly outflow in US dollar terms on record.
insights.locator: ETF weakness was concentrated, not continuous

insights.claim: The World Gold Council reads the H1 2026 US ETF selling as an episodic investment pause rather than a breakdown in the strategic case for gold.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: If correct, the marginal US ETF buyer returns once rates/dollar stabilise — a coiled-spring source of demand into H2.
insights.quote: The concentration of outflows in these two months suggests an episodic investment pause rather than a sustained breakdown in the strategic case for gold.
insights.locator: What drove H1 ETF outflows?

themes.theme: War liquidity, hawkish Fed, firmer dollar

insights.claim: The escalation of the US-Iran war initially caused investors to sell gold to raise liquidity rather than buy it as a hedge, inverting the usual geopolitical safe-haven response.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gold can sell off on the first shock of a conflict as margin and liquidity needs dominate — buy the de-risking, don't chase the headline.
insights.quote: The escalation in geopolitical risk stemming from the US-Iran war initially prompted investors to raise liquidity, while gold’s strong 2025 performance and record highs in early 2026 provided an opportunity to lock in gains or reduce allocations that had risen above target weights
insights.locator: What drove H1 ETF outflows?

insights.claim: Gold's strong 2025 performance and record highs in early 2026 pushed portfolio gold weights above target, making mechanical rebalancing and profit-taking a distinct source of 2026 ETF supply.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Rebalancing-driven selling is price-insensitive and self-limiting — it fades once weights normalise, unlike thesis-driven exits.
insights.locator: De-risking, profit taking and rebalancing

insights.claim: A stronger dollar, higher yields and delayed rate-cut expectations under a more hawkish Fed outlook raised the opportunity cost of holding gold through H1 2026.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: US gold ETF flow remains a rates-and-dollar trade — the flow turns on the first credible Fed easing repricing.
insights.quote: A stronger dollar, higher yields and delayed rate-cut expectations weighed on demand, particularly as markets adopted a more hawkish outlook for Fed policy.
insights.locator: Higher opportunity costs and inflation concerns

insights.claim: By June 2026 investors were pricing the US-Iran conflict mainly through its inflationary consequences — higher yields and a firmer dollar — rather than through gold's safe-haven appeal.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: War-driven inflation is currently bearish for gold via the rates channel; the trade only flips if the Fed is seen accommodating the shock.
insights.quote: By June, investors appeared more focused on the conflict’s inflationary implications, and the potential for higher yields and a firmer dollar, than on gold’s safe-haven appeal
insights.locator: Higher opportunity costs and inflation concerns

insights.claim: The two 2026 outflow episodes had different mechanisms: March was forced de-risking, crowded positioning and momentum-driven liquidation, while June was a fundamental repricing of rates, real yields and the dollar.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Positioning flushes mean-revert quickly; a real-yield repricing does not — the June driver is the one to monitor for whether outflows resume.
insights.quote: In summary, March reflected forced de-risking, crowded positioning and momentum-driven liquidation, whereas June reflected renewed price weakness and a more fundamental repricing of rates, real yields and the dollar.
insights.locator: What drove H1 ETF outflows?

themes.theme: Flagship funds bleed, low-cost siblings gain

insights.claim: Year-to-date through 30 June 2026, GLD saw US$9,021mn of outflows (-65t of holdings) and IAU US$4,168mn (-29t), while lower-cost GLDM took in US$4,317mn (+28t) and IAUM US$837mn (+5t).
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The US 'gold exit' is really a rotation out of the two flagship products into cheaper mini versions — a fee-compression story for State Street and BlackRock, not pure gold de-allocation.
insights.locator: Table 2: Top four US-listed funds based on net inflows

insights.claim: GLD's US$9.0bn of 2026 year-to-date outflows reversed roughly 39% of the US$23,361mn it took in during 2025, while GLDM's YTD inflows already exceed half of its US$8,017mn 2025 haul.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Tactical hot money concentrated in GLD is what left; sticky allocation money in the mini products kept adding — a cleaner read on strategic demand.
insights.locator: Table 2: Top four US-listed funds based on net inflows

insights.claim: Despite 65t of tonnage redemptions, GLD's AUM only fell from US$148bn at end-2025 to US$130bn by 30 June 2026, while GLDM's AUM rose from US$25bn to US$27bn as holdings grew from 183t to 211t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: High gold prices cushion issuer revenue even through heavy redemptions — fee income is far more resilient than the tonnage headlines imply.
insights.locator: Table 2: Top four US-listed funds based on net inflows

insights.claim: Higher gold prices have amplified the US dollar impact of any given tonnage of US ETF outflow, which is why H1 2026 ranks second-worst in dollar terms but only fourth-worst in tonnes.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Dollar-flow headlines will keep looking historically extreme at high prices — use tonnage, not US$bn, to compare flow episodes across cycles.
insights.quote: Chart 2: Higher gold prices amplified the dollar impact of US ETF outflows
insights.locator: Chart 2 heading

themes.theme: Retail bar and coin: two-way, gold over silver

insights.claim: US bar and coin demand was 13.8t in Q2 2026, up 28% y/y but down 20% q/q, as range-bound prices limited buying momentum and sell-back activity moderated from earlier-2026 highs.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: US retail physical demand is quietly the only sector growing y/y — a floor under demand that the ETF-driven headline hides.
insights.quote: Demand increased y/y but remained below Q1 levels, as range-bound prices limited buying momentum and sell-back activity moderated from the elevated levels seen earlier in the year.
insights.locator: US gold demand overshadowed by ETF outflows

insights.claim: North American dealers report that retail trading volumes normalised in Q2 2026 from extraordinary earlier-year levels, with long-term holders taking profits into strength and other buyers adding on price pullbacks.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Two-way retail flow dampens both rallies and selloffs — expect retail to be a stabiliser, not an accelerant, in the next move.
insights.quote: Nevertheless, two-way flows remained a defining feature of the market.
insights.locator: North American retail investment

insights.claim: Dealers report continued retail buying of gold alongside ongoing liquidation of silver, indicating retail investors are actively rotating out of silver into gold.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A negative flow signal for retail silver products and a supportive one for the gold/silver ratio at the physical margin.
insights.quote: Gold continued to attract stronger investor interest than silver, with several market participants reporting ongoing gold purchases alongside continued silver liquidation
insights.locator: North American retail investment

insights.claim: US retail buyers increasingly prefer investment bars over coins to maximise metal exposure per dollar invested, a direct consequence of high bullion prices squeezing premium tolerance.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Premium-heavy coin products lose share as prices rise — negative for mint/numismatic margins, neutral-to-positive for bar fabricators.
insights.quote: Investment bars remained a preferred product among retail investors seeking to maximise metal exposure per dollar invested, reflecting continued sensitivity to higher bullion prices.
insights.locator: North American retail investment

themes.theme: Jewellery bifurcation and tech mix shift

insights.claim: US jewellery demand was 22.2t in Q2 2026, up 65% q/q but down 25% y/y, with value rising y/y even as volumes fell — high prices are converting tonnage into revenue.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Jewellery retailers can post rising revenue on falling gold volumes; don't read tonnage weakness as a sector earnings warning.
insights.quote: Jewellery demand remained weak in volume terms, although value increased y/y.
insights.locator: US gold demand overshadowed by ETF outflows

insights.claim: US gold jewellery weakness is concentrated in the mass market while the high end holds up, with higher-income households taking a larger share of retail gold spend and consumers shifting to lighter-weight, lower-carat products.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A K-shaped consumer read that favours luxury jewellery names over mass-market retailers, and supports lower-gold-content product mix.
insights.quote: Weakness appeared most pronounced in the mass market, while higher-end jewellery remained more resilient, reinforcing the recent trend of higher-income households accounting for a larger share of retail spend.
insights.locator: US gold demand overshadowed by ETF outflows

insights.claim: US technology gold demand was 16.3t in Q2 2026, up 6% y/y but down 11% q/q, with steady electronics growth offset by price-driven weakness in dentistry and other industrial uses.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Electronics is the only structurally growing gold end-use in the US; high prices are permanently thrifting gold out of dental and industrial applications.
insights.quote: Technology demand was supported by steady growth in electronics, although higher prices continued to weigh on dentistry and other industrial uses.
insights.locator: US gold demand overshadowed by ETF outflows

insights.claim: The World Gold Council expects investment — not jewellery or technology — to remain the key source of US gold demand growth, with geopolitical uncertainty supportive but ETF flows still hostage to yields, monetary policy expectations and the dollar.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Position US gold demand recovery as a rates trade: the recovery signal is a dovish Fed repricing or dollar rollover, not a geopolitical headline.
insights.quote: Geopolitical uncertainty should provide support, although ETF flows may remain sensitive to yields, monetary policy expectations and the dollar.
insights.locator: Highlights
